Key Points
The bankruptcy of Claire's is just the latest sign of how long-time retail mall anchors have fallen on hard times.
But as mall tenants change, some are seeing as much as triple the revenue from former Sears or Macy’s locations from bookstores, grocery stores, and even churches that lease square footage.
Visits to enclosed malls remain healthy, in part due to these new attractions.
Brookfield Properties gave the Staten Island Mall's food court a facelift in 2018, with an upgraded look and new restaurants.
Source: Brookfield Properties
The Dayton Mall has been a shopping staple for residents of Dayton, Ohio, since it opened in 1970.  The once-prospering mall, like many, has faced hard times with increased vacancies, exacerbated by the closing of two anchors, Sears and Bon Ton, in 2018.
As a result, the mall was put into receivership, where it remains. But the 162,000-square-foot former Sears space was sold to a local church, Crossroads, which has transformed 90,000 square feet of the former store into a house of worship and community hub with a traditional indoor entrance to the rest of the mall.
"Nothing says dying mall like having a church move in," said Rebecca Maguire, marketing manager of the Dayton Mall. "But Crossroads has a huge following, and they are so community driven that I think any mall in the world would be lucky to have a partner like that."
It's fair to ask if a struggling mall is the right place for a church, and Matt Castleman, the pastor of Crossroads Church in Dayton, said the religious organization had its own reservations.
"People were asking, is chaining yourself to a mall wise?" said Castleman.
The church, part of an eight-church network based in Cincinnati, celebrated its first services on this year's Easter Sunday and has drawn thousands to the once moribund mall. The church also decided to keep the complex open seven days a week, whenever the mall is open.
"We have 400 to 500 people a week pop in who have no affiliation to the church," Castleman said.  Teenagers fan the mall after services to eat at the food court and show back up at the church with bags from stores like Claire's and
Dick's Sporting Goods
, Castleman said.
Of course,
Claire's bankruptcy filing this week
is one more sign of how the hard times for long-time mall tenants are not going away. But filling old anchors with new, niche businesses or destinations, like in the case of the Dayton Mall with its new church tenant, is precisely the type of "cross-shopping" mall landlords are seeking.
While a church is the unconventional salvation of the Dayton Mall, other malls are also finding out-of-the-box suitors to fill big empty spaces.
The fall of the American mall has long been chronicled, and not exactly greatly exaggerated. Enclosed malls with anchor stores, a bustling food court, and a stable of trendy fashion retailers sandwiched between were the centerpiece of post-WWII suburbia for generations. However, changing demographics, shifting shopping habits, and the rise of Amazon and e-commerce all contributed to the decline of malls.
But recent data and industry executives suggest that the enclosed mall could be positioned for a rebirth.
The trend of repurposing empty anchors, which in some cases began a decade ago, took a long time to bear fruit, said Stephen Lebovitz, CEO of CBL Properties, one of the largest mall landlords in the U.S. with more than 155,000,000 square feet of mall space.
"We have had a rebound and built a lot of positive momentum. These projects to backfill anchors don't happen overnight," Lebovitz said. And even when the old anchors were filled relatively quickly, it can take time to break through to customers.
"It has taken several years to recover from anchor closings in 2017-2018," Lebovitz said, referring to a wave of anchors that closed that year. The past decade has seen traditional anchors like
Macy's
, JCPenney, and Sears shutter.
The subdivided mall and 'cross-shopping'
Lebovitz said the key to success is subdividing formerly sprawling anchor stores into niche players that all draw in their cross-shopping constituencies. There are former Sears' locations in the CBL portfolio that were generating $7 million to $8 million a year, with newly filled, subdivided ones bringing in a combined five to six times that amount, according to Lebovitz. A variety of different businesses are filling those voids, from restaurants like The Cheesecake Factory, to large retailers like Dick's Sporting Goods, entertainment options like Dave & Buster's, or hotels.
Lebovitz said that mall developers are also trying to add more experiential categories, such as games, bowling, and laser tag.
Other mall owners are taking it even a step further, converting old stores into
things like apartments
or
large food courts
.

data.title: Ask HN: How can ChatGPT serve 700M users when I can't run one GPT-4 locally?
data.author: superasn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大规模AI模型的推理效率和成本优化

不同观点：
• canyon289认为，Google等大公司有专门的团队研究并优化AI模型的推理效率，并分享了相关技术文档和指南，强调了专业团队在优化上的深度思考。
• airhangerf15指出，高端GPU如H100的成本极高，整个计算集群的构建和维护费用巨大，普通用户难以负担。他还预测，当AI泡沫破裂后，这些设备价格会大幅下降，普通用户才有机会使用。
• piyh强调了大公司如OpenAI在资金和资源上的巨大优势，指出这些公司通过规模效应和大量资金投入实现了个人用户无法企及的效率优化。
• abathologist提到了OpenAI的巨额亏损，暗示高效的大规模推理系统背后是高昂的研发成本。
• fergal_reid解释了批量处理（batching）在提高推理效率上的重要性，并分享了相关技术博客，指出大公司可能拥有更高级的专有技术。

补充讨论：
• joshhart详细描述了多种技术优化手段，如8位浮点数压缩、专家混合模型（Mixture of Experts）、推测解码（speculative decoding）等，以提高推理效率。
• jp57指出，虽然OpenAI有7亿用户，但多数用户的使用频率不高，导致计算资源在多数时间处于闲置状态，从而提高了整体效率。
• ritz_labringue也提到了专家混合模型和推测解码，强调了大公司在硬件和软件优化上的综合优势，使得个人用户难以复制这些优化。
• roadside_picnic和ryao进一步解释了推测解码和快速转发的技术细节，以及它们在推理速度上的显著提升。
• Szpadel重申了批量处理在提高效率上的核心作用，但也指出这在延迟和吞吐量之间需要权衡。
• venusenvy47强调了大公司通过并行处理多用户请求来最大化利用GPU和内存。
• mquander以较为简单的语言解释了推理过程中的并行处理和缓存利用，强调了多用户请求同时处理的优势。
• rythie认为，普通用户可以在本地运行一些较小规模的模型，并推测OpenAI可能使用较旧的GPU集群进行推理，同时提到公司可能使用排队系统来分配任务。
• dcreater总结了三点：1) 用户不同时使用，2) 普通用户可以本地运行GPT-4等效模型，3) 需要大量工程优化，但云计算时代提供了更多可能性。

争议焦点：
• 普通用户是否能在本地高效运行大规模AI模型。

data.title: All About Transformer Inference
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Transformer模型的推理过程，强调其与训练的不同之处，特别是对延迟的考虑。推理涉及两个主要步骤：**Prefill**和**Generation**。Prefill处理输入提示并保存中间激活值（即键值缓存），而Generation则基于缓存逐个生成新词。为了提高效率，使用键值缓存避免重复计算，将时间复杂度从$O(n^2)$和$O(n^3)$降低到$O(n)$和$O(n^2)$。推理优化需关注延迟，包括首 token 生成时间（TTFT）和每 token 的延迟，特别是在线聊天和流媒体任务对低延迟要求较高。相比训练，推理在处理大规模模型时引入了新的复杂性和挑战。

44845497.article_content:
All About Transformer Inference
Part 7 of
How To Scale Your Model
(
Part 6: Training LLaMA
|
Part 8: Serving LLaMA
)
Performing inference on a Transformer can be very different from training. Partly this is because inference adds a new factor to consider: latency. In this section, we will go all the way from sampling a single new token from a model to efficiently scaling a large Transformer across many slices of accelerators as part of an inference engine.
The Basics of Transformer Inference
So you’ve trained a Transformer, and you want to use it to generate some new sequences.
At the end of the day, benchmark scores going up and loss curves going down are only proxies for whether something interesting is going to happen once the rubber hits the road!
Historically, you can do a surprising amount of research on Transformers without ever touching inference — LLM loss, multiple choice benchmarks can be run efficiently without a proper KV cache or generation loop implementation. This meant, especially in research codebases, there's often a lot of low hanging fruits in the inference codepath.
Sampling is conceptually simple. We put a sequence in and our favorite Transformer will spit out \(\log p(\text{next token}_i \vert \text{previous tokens})\), i.e. log-probabilities for all possible next tokens. We can sample from this distribution and obtain a new token. Append this token and repeat this process and we obtain a sequence of tokens which is a continuation of the prompt.
Figure:
naive sampling from a Transformer. The blue logits give us a distribution over the next token that we can sample from. Note that each step re-processes the entire prefix, leading to a $\Theta(n^2)$ runtime for the algorithm.
We have just described the naive implementation of Transformer sampling, and while it works,
we never do it in practice
because we are re-processing the entire sequence every time we generate a token. This algorithm is \(O(n^2)\) on the FFW and \(O(n^3)\) on the attention mechanism to generate \(n\) tokens!
How do we avoid this?
Instead of doing the full forward pass every time, it turns out we can save some intermediate activations from each forward pass that let us avoid re-processing previous tokens. Specifically, since a given token only attends to previous tokens during dot-product attention, we can simply write each token’s key and value projections into a new data structure called a
KV cache
. Once we’ve saved these key/value projections for past tokens, future tokens can simply compute their \(q_i \cdot k_j\) products without performing any new FLOPs on the earlier tokens. Amazing!
With this in mind, inference has two key parts:
Prefill
: Given a long prompt, we process all the tokens in the prompt at the same time and save the resulting activations (specifically, the key-value projections) in a
“KV cache”
. We also save the logits for the last token.
Generation
: Given a KV cache and the previous logits, we incrementally sample one token from the logits, feed that token back into the Transformer, and produce a new set of logits for the next step. We also append the KV activations for that new token to the KV cache. We repeat this until we hit a special
<EOS>
token or reach some maximum length limit.
Here’s a diagram of sampling with a KV cache:
Figure:
diagram of efficient Transformer sampling with a KV cache.
Prefill
processes our prompt and saves all the per-token key-value activations in a cache.
Generation
takes this cache (and the last-token logits), samples a new token, and passes that new token through the model, attending to the KV cache and saving the new token's key-value projections back to the cache. This is an $O(n)$ algorithm in the MLP block.
By sampling with a KV cache, we’ve reduced our time complexity to generate $n$ tokens to \(O(n)\) on the FFW and \(O(n^2)\) on the attention, since we never reprocess a previous token. However, many forward passes are still needed to generate a sequence — that’s what’s happening when you query Gemini or ChatGPT and the result streams back to you. Every token is (usually) a separate (but partially cached) Transformer call to a massive model.
We will soon see that
prefill
and
generation
are very different beasts —— Transformer inference is two tasks in disguise! Compared to training, the KV cache is also a novel and significant source of complexity.
What do we actually want to optimize?
Before we proceed further, it’s worth highlighting one aspect of inference that’s totally new: latency. While during training we only care about throughput (total tokens processed per second), during inference we have to worry about how fast we’re producing tokens (both the
Time To First Token (TTFT)
and the
per-token latency
). For example:
Offline batch inference
for evals and data generation only cares about bulk cost of inference and is blind to the latency of individual samples.
Chat interfaces/streaming tasks

data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: AOL宣布将终止其拨号上网服务，这一服务已有四十多年历史，曾为数千万人提供了早期互联网接入。该服务将于2025年9月30日正式停止，包括AOL Dialer和AOL Shield等相关软件也将下线。AOL未详细说明关闭原因，但显然由于更快捷的互联网连接方式已普及，拨号上网已过时。AOL曾是互联网时代的先驱，尤其在1990年代广受欢迎，拥有数百万用户，并进行了多次收购。然而，随着宽带和移动互联网的兴起，拨号服务逐渐衰退，尽管仍有少量用户依赖此服务。此次关闭标志着一个时代的终结。

44849016.article_content:
More than 40 years after starting as a very early Apple service, AOL is finally ending its dial-up Internet service, shuttering a service that helped usher in the Internet age for tens of millions of people around the world.
Older
Mac
users will remember the early days of the Internet and the dominance of AOL. Decades later, the circle has closed as AOL says it will start to shut down its dial-up Internet service.
On a
support page
titled "Dial-up Internet to be discontinued," updated on August 8, AOL warns that it has decided to end its dial-up service. It will no longer make dial-up available via AOL plans.
On September 30, 2025, AOL says that its dial-up service and associated software, the AOL Dialer and AOL Shield, will be discontinued. The shutdown will not affect any other AOL plan benefits that users may continue to use.
As for why dial-up is being shuttered, AOL says it "routinely evaluates its products and services," but doesn't disclose why it decided to discontinue dial-up access. The most obvious reason is due to the ubiquity of other, considerably faster, connections available to almost everyone.
That doesn't take away the fact that AOL was how millions of people were introduced to the Internet.
First-mover dominance
Back in the late 1980s, the Internet wasn't a digital utility as it is now. There was no cellular Internet, no smartphones, and a telecommunications infrastructure not built for digital communications.
Connecting to the Internet was hard, as you had to use a modem with a phone line that communicated at very slow speeds. Not to mention a fairly difficult process to set up the connection, and that the World Wide Web was only just starting to become a thing.
AOL itself started back in 1983 under the name Control Video Corporation, offering online services for the Atari 2600 console. After failing, it became Quantum Computer Services in 1985, eventually launching AppleLink in 1988 to connect Macintosh computers together.
Our Managing Editor Mike Wuerthele was working at an Apple dealership in the late eighties, and used Apple Link there.
With the launch of PC Link for IBM-compatible PCs in 1988 and parting from Apple in October 1989, the company rebranded itself as America Online, or AOL. Unlike the rival incumbent Compuserve, AOL was pitched as a user-friendly way for non-technical people to get on the Internet.
It was still a far cry from the hyper-speed connectivity available now. Even at its height, dial-up connections could get up to 56 kilobits per second under ideal conditions, while modern connections are measured in megabits and gigabits.
The 90's era logo for AOL
Most of the service was also what's considered a "walled garden," with features that were only available through AOL itself and that it wasn't the actual, untamed Internet.
The rebrand and refocus was a decision that paid off, and allowed AOL to grow considerably within a few years.
In the 1990s, AOL grew along with the wider use of computers, thanks to the introduction of graphical operating systems and other elements. There was also a period when AOL became well-known for distributing so many CDs containing AOL trials for its marketing.
Millions signed up, with it counting ten million customers by 1995.
The sheer number of users led to massive financial success and inevitable acquisitions. This included WebCrawler in 1995, eWorld in 1996, and competitor
CompuServe in 1998
.
Broadband and decline
In the 2000s, other forms of connectivity than dial-up started to become more prevalent. Cable Internet services, among others, were cropping up in major cities.
These faster connections were a credible threat to dial-up services, and started to pull customers away. Later in the decade, cellular connectivity became another danger for dial-up services, led by Apple's
iPhone
.
With the ease of access available from smartphones, as well as the growing availability of broadband services at home and at work, dial-up's days were numbered.
However, while depreciated by society, dial-up still had its uses. Low-income families or those who lived in rural areas where broadband wasn't an option could still use dial-up to get online.
Even after the AOL Time Warner acquisition and the 2015 acquisition by Verizon, AOL was still a popular service. Astoundingly, it counted about two million dial-up subscribers at the time.
Despite managing to still have a significant number of dial-up users, that wouldn't be for too long.
In the 2021 acquisition of
assets from Verizon
by Apollo Global Management, AOL was said to have 1.5 million people paying for services. However, this was more for technical support and software, rather than for actual Internet access.
A
CNBC
report
at the time reports that the dial-up user count was "in the low thousands."
The writing has been on the wall for a long time for AOL's dial-up service. Ending the service was an inevitability, albeit one that has taken far longer than many would expect.

data.title: Getting good results from Claude Code
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
本文总结了作者使用Claude Code编程代理的经验。作者在几个月内利用Claude Code快速完成了约12个编程项目，认为没有它无法在相同时间内完成这些工作。虽然AI生成的代码常有错误或低效，但作者强调自己对最终代码负责，因此会手动审查和测试所有AI编写的代码。

作者分享了获得良好结果的关键方法：提前写清需求文档以提供上下文，准备项目结构和运行指南，让代理自我代码审查，以及使用个人“全局”代理指南。该指南强调增量进展、学习现有代码、 pragmatic approach、简单设计和测试驱动开发等原则，并提供问题解决流程和代码质量标准。作者还提出在遇到困难时最多尝试三次，然后重新评估问题。

总的来说，尽管使用Claude Code有挑战，但通过合理的策略和手动审查，可以显著提高编程效率。

• [aosaigh] 持相反观点，认为清晰的规范文档对于Claude的成功使用至关重要。他通过详细的12步文档节省了大量时间，并认为中级和高级开发者仍不可替代，因为需要他们来制定明确的实施步骤。

44836879.article_content:
I've been experimenting with LLM programming agents over the past few months. Claude Code has become my favorite.
It is not without issues, but it's allowed me to write ~12 programs/projects in relatively little time, and I feel I would not have been able to do all this in the same amount of time without it. Most of them, I wouldn't even have bothered to write without Claude Code, simply because they'd take too much of my time. (A list is included at the end of this post.)
I'm still far from a Claude Code expert, and I have a backlog of blog posts and documentation to review that might be useful. But — and this is critical — you don't have to read everything that's out there to start seeing results. You don't even need to read
this
post; just type some prompts in and see what comes out.
That said, because I just wrote this up for a job application,
here's how I'm getting good results from Claude Code
. I've embedded links to some examples where appropriate.
A key is writing a clear spec ahead of time, which provides context to the agent as it works in the codebase.
Having a document for the agent that outlines the project’s structure and how to run e.g. builds and linters is helpful.
Asking the agent to perform a code review on its own work is surprisingly fruitful.
Finally, I have a personal “global” agent guide describing best practices for agents to follow, specifying things like problem-solving approach, use of TDD, etc.
(This file is listed near the end of this post.)
Then there's the question of
validating LLM-written code.
AI-generated code
is
often incorrect or inefficient.
It’s important for me to call out that
I believe I’m ultimately responsible for the code that goes into a PR with my name on it, regardless of how it was produced
.
Therefore, especially in any professional context, I manually review all AI-written code and test cases. I’ll add test cases for anything I think is missing or needs improvement, either manually or by asking the LLM to write those cases (which I then review).
At the end of the day, manual review is necessary to verify that behavior is implemented correctly and tested properly.
Personal "global" agent guide
This lives at
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
:
# Development Guidelines
## Philosophy
### Core Beliefs
- **Incremental progress over big bangs** - Small changes that compile and pass tests
- **Learning from existing code** - Study and plan before implementing
- **Pragmatic over dogmatic** - Adapt to project reality
- **Clear intent over clever code** - Be boring and obvious
### Simplicity Means
- Single responsibility per function/class
- Avoid premature abstractions
- No clever tricks - choose the boring solution
- If you need to explain it, it's too complex
## Process
### 1. Planning & Staging
Break complex work into 3-5 stages. Document in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`:
```markdown
## Stage N: [Name]
**Goal**: [Specific deliverable]
**Success Criteria**: [Testable outcomes]
**Tests**: [Specific test cases]
**Status**: [Not Started|In Progress|Complete]
```
- Update status as you progress
- Remove file when all stages are done
### 2. Implementation Flow
1. **Understand** - Study existing patterns in codebase
2. **Test** - Write test first (red)
3. **Implement** - Minimal code to pass (green)
4. **Refactor** - Clean up with tests passing
5. **Commit** - With clear message linking to plan
### 3. When Stuck (After 3 Attempts)
**CRITICAL**: Maximum 3 attempts per issue, then STOP.
1. **Document what failed**:
- What you tried
- Specific error messages
- Why you think it failed
2. **Research alternatives**:
- Find 2-3 similar implementations
- Note different approaches used
3. **Question fundamentals**:
- Is this the right abstraction level?
- Can this be split into smaller problems?
- Is there a simpler approach entirely?
4. **Try different angle**:
- Different library/framework feature?
- Different architectural pattern?
- Remove abstraction instead of adding?
## Technical Standards
### Architecture Principles
- **Composition over inheritance** - Use dependency injection
- **Interfaces over singletons** - Enable testing and flexibility
- **Explicit over implicit** - Clear data flow and dependencies
- **Test-driven when possible** - Never disable tests, fix them
### Code Quality
- **Every commit must**:
- Compile successfully
- Pass all existing tests
- Include tests for new functionality
- Follow project formatting/linting
- **Before committing**:
- Run formatters/linters
- Self-review changes
- Ensure commit message explains "why"
### Error Handling
- Fail fast with descriptive messages
- Include context for debugging
- Handle errors at appropriate level
- Never silently swallow exceptions
## Decision Framework
When multiple valid approaches exist, choose based on:
1. **Testability** - Can I easily test this?
2. **Readability** - Will someone understand this in 6 months?
3. **Consistency** - Does this match project patterns?
4. **Simplicity** - Is this the simplest solution that wo

本文总结了作者使用Claude Code编程代理的经验。作者在几个月内利用Claude Code快速完成了约12个编程项目，认为没有它无法在相同时间内完成这些工作。虽然AI生成的代码常有错误或低效，但作者强调自己对最终代码负责，因此会手动审查和测试所有AI编写的代码。

作者分享了获得良好结果的关键方法：提前写清需求文档以提供上下文，准备项目结构和运行指南，让代理自我代码审查，以及使用个人“全局”代理指南。该指南强调增量进展、学习现有代码、 pragmatic approach、简单设计和测试驱动开发等原则，并提供问题解决流程和代码质量标准。作者还提出在遇到困难时最多尝试三次，然后重新评估问题。

总的来说，尽管使用Claude Code有挑战，但通过合理的策略和手动审查，可以显著提高编程效率。

data.title: Abusing Entra OAuth for fun and access to internal Microsoft applications
data.author: the1bernard
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者如何意外获取微软内部22个服务的访问权限。作者在写文档时，注意到微软的短链接服务aka.ms，并好奇访问其主页，发现一个登录界面。经过多次尝试，作者通过一个多租户配置错误的工程中心应用，成功访问了微软内部工程门户，查看到大量敏感信息。该问题源于Entra ID在多租户应用中的认证和授权处理不当，导致外部用户可通过同意提示获取内部访问权限。作者随后向微软安全响应中心报告了该问题，并探讨了其他可能受影响的微软服务。
data.comments_summary:

• Fock询问该问题是否有CVE编号，担心云计划不会注意到此问题。

• 争议的焦点在于Entra ID和OAuth2在多租户应用授权中的复杂性及安全性问题，尤其是验证流程的不充分性。

• 对微软在处理安全漏洞时的奖励政策也有所不满，尤其是对严重漏洞发现者未给予奖励的情况。

Consent & Compromise: Abusing Entra OAuth for Fun and Access to Internal Microsoft Applications
Aug 7, 2025
By:
Vaisha Bernard
This blog is about how I got access to over 22 internal Microsoft services and how you might be vulnerable too.
After my
last talk at the 38C3 conference in Hamburg
, this was the top comment on YouTube.
Well, this story definitely falls in the category “someone stumbling around finding horrifying vulnerabilities”. Although this time I was not even having issues, I was just distracted from a boring task.
You see, I was writing some documentation the other day, when my Eye fell on one of those aka.ms links. For those of you who don’t know, aka.ms is the
URL shortener service used by Microsoft
.
My mind started to wonder. Where would you end up if you would just visit
https://aka.ms
, so without any shortener link included?
A login screen. This is probably where Microsoft employees manage their links. I did wonder though, what would happen if I simply tried logging in here myself with my own Microsoft account? Surely, that would not work, right?
Of course not! You need an account in the Microsoft tenant, otherwise, no luck. Back to writing that boring documentation. But what was that?
An indexing service for aka.ms links
? Interesting.
And one of those links points to an eng.ms domain. What is that?
Another login screen! It did not work the first time, but maybe I can login here! The result surprised me.
I got a consent prompt, asking me to give consent to share my basic profile information with this application. Sure, why not? Does that mean this is an application I can access?
After clicking “accept”, I get a 500 Internal Server Error message. I’m pretty sure that was this server trying to tell me that this application was not meant to be accessed by me. But now I’m intrigued, what is eng.ms? I still had that documentation to write, but that had to wait.
I started subdomain enumeration on the domain eng.ms and found an interesting subdomain: rescue.eng.ms. This gave me another login screen and another consent prompt. But this time it gave me access using my own Microsoft 365 account! Notice my name in the upper right corner?
I quickly realized that I should not have access here. This Engineering Hub was some sort of portal for Microsoft Engineers. I must admit, my knee-jerk reaction as a red-teamer was to search for the phrase “password”. What can I say, I could not help myself. It returned 13,252 hits, all referring to internal Microsoft procedures and product groups. I was clearly not supposed to access this.
I stopped here and reported this to the Microsoft Security Response Centre (MSRC). But what had happened here? Why was I able to access this internal portal and might other services be vulnerable in the same way?
To answer that question, we need to have a closer look at how Entra ID handles authentication and authorization for multi-tenant applications.
Multi-Tenant Applications
When developers want to use Entra for authentication to a web application, the application needs to first be registered at Entra. This is called an “App Registration” or “Application Object”. These applications can be set to accept users from the tenant where they are registered (single-tenant), or users from any tenant (multi-tenant). They can also be configured to accept “personal Microsoft accounts”.
App developers are then tasked to configure the authorization server (login.microsoftonline.com in most cases) in application logic and all four options above have a corresponding desired value for the authorization server URL.
So single-tenant applications should be configured to use
https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenantid>
or
https://login.microsoftonline.com/<domain>
as the authorization server, while multi-tenant applications that also accept personal Microsoft accounts should use
https://login.microsoftonline.com/common
.
The Engineering Hub was configured as a multi-tenant application and redirected me to the /common endpoint.
This allowed me to login (step 1 & 2) with my own “work or school account”, which triggered a Consent prompt (Step 3), as the application was not used in my own tenant before. When I gave it consent, it was instantiated into a Service Principal or “Enterprise Application” (step 4) in my own tenant and returned an access token (step 5).
This access token was issued by my own tenant. The “iss” (issuer) and “tid” (tenant ID) claims were set to values corresponding with my own tenant. Any conditional access policies or user assignment took place in my own tenant according to my own configuration. I was authenticated & authorized, only by the wrong authority. And nowhere in application logic was this checked.
This made me wonder. What other Microsoft services could be impacted by this misconfiguration? Let’s find out!
Mapping the Microsoft Attack Surface

• 另一个值得注意的点是对云安全和传统网络安全措施的讨论，强调了仅依赖认证token的潜在风险。
• 对微软在处理安全漏洞时的奖励政策也有所不满，尤其是对严重漏洞发现者未给予奖励的情况。

data.title: GPT-5: Overdue, overhyped and underwhelming. And that's not the worst of it
data.author: kgwgk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT-5的表现及其相关评论和批评的合理性

不同观点：
• **Uehreka**：认为文章过于依赖社交媒体反应，缺乏作者自身的深入分析，且表达方式过于偏颇，既不算新闻报道，也不算深度分析。
• **chmod775**：批评GPT-5在面对不确定问题时无法坦诚表示“不知道”，导致用户浪费时间。认为这是目前GPT模型最大的改进点。
• **TulliusCicero**：反驳文章中对无人驾驶汽车技术的批评，认为尽管技术发展比预期慢，但在一些城市中已经取得了显著进展，不再是不切实际的幻想。
• **mikert89**：指出文章未提及GPT-5 Pro模型，并认为OpenAI为了追求用户增长和与谷歌竞争，而未进入高性能、高成本的市场领域。
• **computegabe**：认为GPT-5无法满足公众过高的期望，这些期望因模因和炒作而被放大。OpenAI应拒绝这种炒作，专注于渐进改进。
• **mentalgear**：支持Gary Marcus的批评，认为AI社区需要更多像他这样的独立专家来保持透明度和诚信，并指出Marcus在多个前沿问题上已被证明正确。
• **starchild3001**：引用Gemini 2.5 Pro的回应来支持Gary Marcus的文章，但同时认为Marcus对AI的看法可能已经过时，并讨论了模型延迟对用户体验的影响。
• **resters**：对GPT-5持积极态度，认为其在代码调试和研究反馈方面提供了高质量的帮助，是 lineup 中的一个重要补充。
• **hexage1814**：认为Gary Marcus的文章过于耸人听闻，像是在为了反对而反对，而不是提出建设性的批评。
• **Havoc**：认为Gary Marcus对Altman和GPT-5的批评是出于个人恩怨，并认为GPT-5的增量改进是正常的，不应过度苛责。
• **SerCe**：列举了GPT-5在实际使用中的问题，包括响应质量下降和自定义GPT功能失效，认为这是一次巨大的降级。
• **wbharding**：认为Gary Marcus的文章总是能找到新的“问题”，并预测这些问题将在下一个版本中被修复，同时认为AI技术的进展被过度夸大。
• **calrain**：指出GPT-5在对话中容易突然失去上下文，需要用户手动提示才能继续有效对话。
• **kylecazar**：认为文章最有价值的部分是提醒人们管理对AI技术的期望，GPT-5只是增量进步，而不是奇迹。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：GPT-5是否如宣传的那样具有突破性进展，还是仅仅是增量改进。
- **模型性能问题**：包括无法承认无知、对话中失去上下文、延迟问题和自定义功能失效等实际使用中的问题。
- **市场策略**：OpenAI是否为了增长而忽视了高性能市场，以及是否参与了过度的市场炒作。
- **AI技术进展**：是否如一些评论所说，AI技术进展被过度夸大，或是如Marcus所批评的那样存在方向性问题。

data.title: How I code with AI on a budget/free
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型使用与优化、免费资源获取、本地开发环境搭建

不同观点：
• [radio879的观点] 强调使用多种AI模型（如GLM-4.5、Kimi K2、Qwen3-Coder等）在代理环境中的有效性，并介绍了自己开发的辅助应用（https://wuu73.org/aicp），用于在不同AI聊天界面和IDE之间跳转，减少操作摩擦。该应用可以保存项目状态、自动扫描代码文件等，提升工作效率。同时，指出过度依赖API和大型模型会增加成本，而使用较小的模型和免费资源可以实现无限制的编码工作。

• [andai的观点] 认为小型模型在处理简单任务时更有效，因为速度更快。与radio879不同，他更关注“能完成任务的最小模型”，并提出如果放弃代理模式，即使是100倍小的模型也能处理任务。他还提到将整个代码库放入提示中，避免文件系统操作，并测试廉价模型用于代码搜索。

• [sublinear的观点] 认为所有这些AI辅助工具过于复杂，不如自己写代码更直接。

• [yichuan的观点] 提出本地“Cursor-like”栈的潜力，完全在本地运行，无需云和API密钥。建议的设置包括Cursor CLI、本地内存层（如LEANN或Milvus）和本地运行的推理引擎（如Ollama）。虽然需要一些设置 effort，但能实现离线、私有、快速的开发环境。

• [qustrolabe的观点] 认为有些人愿意为免费层放弃数据隐私，虽然自托管需要大量资源，但最终代码会开源，因此可以接受。

• [joshdavham的观点] 同意在AI聊天界面解决问题和提出方案的效果通常优于代理框架（如Cline、Trae、Copilot等）。

补充讨论：
• 免费资源：[chromaton] 提到Google的Gemini提供高限额的免费访问；[reactordev] 推荐Continue.dev和ollama/lmstudio用于本地模型运行；[hgarg] 推荐Rovodev CLI，提供每天2000万个免费token。
• 本地模型运行：[yichuan] 和 [xvv] 讨论了在本地运行模型的可行性和最佳选择，特别是内存和显存限制下的最佳模型。
• 实际应用：[tonyhart7] 提到使用Kiro Code的SDD进行多模型切换；[bravesoul2] 推荐Windsurf的免费模型用于自动完成工作。

争议焦点：
• 使用大型模型与小型模型的优劣：radio879和andai对模型大小的选择和使用场景有不同看法。前者认为大型模型在代理环境中表现更好，而后者则偏向于小型模型以提高速度和效率。
• AI工具的复杂性：sublinear认为AI辅助工具过于复杂，不如手写代码直接，与其他评论者对工具效率的肯定形成对比。

data.title: GPTs and Feeling Left Behind
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 作者描述了对使用AI编程工具的挫败感。尽管看到许多关于AI编写代码的宣传，但作者亲身体验后发现这些工具并不如宣传的那样有效。简单的任务如补全单词或查找函数注释还能胜任，但处理复杂代码时，AI常常生成无用或错误的代码，且容易引入新的错误。尽管如此，作者看到其他人分享的成功案例，尤其是来自有经验的开发者，这让他感到困惑和压力，仿佛自己的技能很快会被淘汰。然而，他自己的使用体验却像在使用一个精美但无实际用途的纸锤子，无法真正解决问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（如ChatGPT、Claude等）在软件开发中的实际应用价值及其局限性

不同观点：
• **LLM在开发中的实用性**：
   - [avalys] 认为LLM（如Cursor）在处理重复性、繁琐的开发任务（如设置构建系统、编写样板代码等）时非常有用，特别是在集成开发环境（IDE）中使用时，能显著提高效率。
   - [martinald] 分享了自己使用Claude Code的经历，强调LLM可以快速完成一些视觉设计和文档更新任务，极大减少了手工工作量，同时还能作为“橡皮鸭”帮助理解代码问题。
   - [allenu] 同样对Claude Code的快速原型开发能力表示认可，特别是在处理API和框架问题时能节省大量时间。

• **LLM在复杂任务中的局限性**：
   - [tyfighter] 指出在C++和GPU驱动开发等特定领域，LLM的帮助有限，可能因为这些领域需要深度的专业知识和理解。
   - [PaulHoule] 强调LLM有时有效，有时无效，成功与否具有随机性，且不同模型和提示技巧可能会影响结果。
   - [storus] 提到LLM引入的细微错误可能很难被发现，导致潜在问题，特别是在与不熟悉的API或库交互时。

• **LLM工具的选择和使用技巧的重要性**：
   - [jackdawed] 分享了一个博客链接，指出通过LLM提问并思考产品需求（PRD/spec）有助于提高系统设计能力。
   - [jtfrench] 认为ChatGPT在复杂代码生成任务中表现不佳，推荐使用Gemini Pro 2.5等其他模型。
   - [calrain] 强调掌握LLM的使用需要时间，类似于学习Vim，需要掌握提示构建和指导AI的技巧。

• **对LLM和AI工具的观望态度**：
   - [SoftTalker] 表示由于AI工具发展太快，目前不愿投入时间尝试，等技术稳定后再考虑使用。
   - [CityOfThrowaway] 指出使用不同的模型和工具（如Claude Code vs gpt-4o）会带来截然不同的体验，强调选择合适的工具至关重要。

补充讨论：
• **FOMO效应和AI工具的营销策略**：
   - [zmmmmm] 认为当前的AI工具炒作存在FOMO营销策略，建议用户不要盲目跟风，而是根据兴趣和需求逐步探索。
   - [dumbmrblah] 强调讨论中应包含使用的模型和提示的具体参数，以避免因不同模型和提示导致的结果差异。

争议焦点：
• **LLM在实际开发中的可靠性和随机性**：部分用户（如[PaulHoule]、[storus]）指出LLM生成代码的质量存在不稳定性，可能引入错误。而其他用户（如[avalys]、[martinald]）则强调LLM在提高效率方面的实际价值。这种分歧反映了LLM在开发中的应用仍具有一定的不确定性。

44851214.article_content:
Every time that I read some blog post about “coding with AI”, or how cool new
models write entire libraries by themselves, I feel like I’m lagging behind,
like I’m missing out on some big, useful tool, and my skills are about to become
obsolete very soon.
So I try different models and tools, and it’s all incredibly underwhelming. It’s
honestly hard to believe that people get work done using these tools, because I
can spend a few hours on them (without getting even close to finishing the task
at hand) and realise that I could have done it myself in 25 minutes.
I tell myself
“learning to use Vim took a long time, but then it paid off”
eventually. But I could (slowly) write text with Vim the first day. I can spend
an entire day with a GPT and produce nothing of value.
GPTs work great for finding the exact word to complete a sentence. They’re
surprisingly good at finding the exact type annotation for a Python function.
They can find nuanced bugs in a single function which I copy-paste into the GPT.
But anything beyond writing a simple function always leads to useless junk.
Often times, they solve big problems by just importing a library that does not
exist, and calling a function which does the bulk of the logic. ChatGPT told me
the other day “if you don’t want any dependencies, you’re going to have to
implement it yourself”. But couldn’t actually implement the necessary code.
Large portions of code have lots of hidden logic bugs, and when they fix one
they introduce another.
And then I see another post on Hacker News, about somebody using GPTs and how
they achieved great results on this and that. Part of me wants to think that
those articles are fake to generate hype, but the reality is that several of
them are written by well-known developers who’ve been around for over a decade.
Some of the results are actually publicly available online.
I’m in a state where I can’t reconcile my own results with other people’s
results. I hear people saying
“this hammer is indestructible”
, but when I pick
it up, it’s just origami: made of paper, intricate, delicate, very cool-looking
but I can’t even hammer a tomato with it.

   - [storus] 提到LLM引入的细微错误可能很难被发现，导致潜在问题，特别是在与不熟悉的API或库交互时。

• **LLM工具的选择和使用技巧的重要性**：
   - [jackdawed] 分享了一个博客链接，指出通过LLM提问并思考产品需求（PRD/spec）有助于提高系统设计能力。
   - [jtfrench] 认为ChatGPT在复杂代码生成任务中表现不佳，推荐使用Gemini Pro 2.5等其他模型。
   - [calrain] 强调掌握LLM的使用需要时间，类似于学习Vim，需要掌握提示构建和指导AI的技巧。

• **对LLM和AI工具的观望态度**：
   - [SoftTalker] 表示由于AI工具发展太快，目前不愿投入时间尝试，等技术稳定后再考虑使用。
   - [CityOfThrowaway] 指出使用不同的模型和工具（如Claude Code vs gpt-4o）会带来截然不同的体验，强调选择合适的工具至关重要。

补充讨论：
• **FOMO效应和AI工具的营销策略**：
   - [zmmmmm] 认为当前的AI工具炒作存在FOMO营销策略，建议用户不要盲目跟风，而是根据兴趣和需求逐步探索。
   - [dumbmrblah] 强调讨论中应包含使用的模型和提示的具体参数，以避免因不同模型和提示导致的结果差异。

争议焦点：
• **LLM在实际开发中的可靠性和随机性**：部分用户（如[PaulHoule]、[storus]）指出LLM生成代码的质量存在不稳定性，可能引入错误。而其他用户（如[avalys]、[martinald]）则强调LLM在提高效率方面的实际价值。这种分歧反映了LLM在开发中的应用仍具有一定的不确定性。

data.title: Happy BuyNothing Day
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于购物体验和购物冲动的不同观点和方法

不同观点：
• [mgkimsal] 提出一个想法：创建一种会员制商店，顾客可以像正常购物一样浏览和试用商品，但不实际支付和带走商品。这种体验的“高潮”在于完成结账步骤，而不是实际拥有商品。他们认为这种模式可以帮助那些购物成瘾的人。

• [redhale] 分享了自己的方法：通过创建一个“想要购买”的待办事项列表来获得购物带来的短暂满足感，而不实际花钱。定期回顾这个列表并删除不再需要的物品，偶尔才会购买真正需要的商品。

• [hilsdev] 通过购买贵金属币来满足自己的购物欲望，这不仅提供了情感上的满足，还带来了投资回报，使购物行为更加理性和有意义。

• [RyanOD] 通过考虑未来子女需要处理遗物的问题来抑制自己的购物欲望，从而避免购买不必要的物品。

• [cnst] 通过寻找高性价比和高品质的商品来对抗购物成瘾。他们使用比价网站寻找符合特定规格和价格的商品，并通过理性分析来判断是否值得购买。

补充讨论：
• [mysterydip] 提到高价商品（如170美元的飞盘）的例子，暗示高价商品可能带来的购物冲动。

• [karim79] 对某款商品的价格提出意见，表示会等待打折再购买，显示出对价格敏感的购物策略。

• [abhinai] 建议扩展商品选择，甚至引入人工智能生成的设计，让人们可以浏览无尽的商品目录，进一步发展原始想法。

• [bookofjoe] 引用了“Reverend Billy and the Church of Stop Shopping”作为一个相关的文化现象，暗示对购物成瘾的批判和反思。

• [jan_Sate] 认为在网站上点击浏览很有趣，但否认自己对在线购物上瘾，显示出对购物体验的享受而不一定是实际购买。

• [Waterluvian] 幽默地指出，无论年龄多大，都可以享受“玩商店”的乐趣。

• [dmoy] 将这种体验比作尼古丁贴片，提供了类似的多巴胺刺激而不损害钱包。

• [coffeecoders] 建议增加商品描述页面、画廊和评论等功能，以增强网站的互动性。

• [Null-Set] 担心这种模式可能会跟踪用户行为并出售给广告商，引发隐私问题。

• [AndrewKemendo] 建议通过发送明信片来完成多巴胺循环，进一步提升购物体验，强调了购物后获得实物（如包裹）的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 购物体验的本质：是实际拥有商品带来的满足感，还是购物过程本身带来的刺激更重要。
• 隐私问题：这种模式是否会侵犯用户隐私，将用户行为数据出售给广告商。

data.title: R0ML's Ratio
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种用于评估批量采购的分析工具，称为“R0ML比率”（RR），由作者的父亲提出。该方法帮助判断批量采购协议是否划算。具体来说，RR通过比较“全额零售价总值”（FURLPoUU）和“批量授权总价”（TPotEEVLA）来评估交易。公式为：RR = TPotEEVLA / FURLPoUU。如果RR小于1，表示交易划算；如果大于1，则意味着采购过多，价值不高。文章以购买1万个红鼻子为 clowns为例，说明如何应用该比率。若所有 clowns 都使用鼻子，RR为0.5，交易值得做；但若仅200个 clowns 使用，RR则为25，交易不划算。该方法尤其适用于软件和SaaS采购，以避免浪费资金。作者建议，在不确定使用量时，先小规模采购以避免成为“冤大头”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：企业采购中的大批量购买与折扣的利弊

不同观点：
• **osener的观点**：在企业中进行采购往往涉及繁琐的流程。他分享了一个团队想尝试A/B测试，但在选择SaaS工具时经历了漫长的采购流程，最终签署了三年企业合同。然而，当合同签订时，原团队已经解散，导致资源浪费。这说明了企业采购流程的复杂性和潜在的低效。

• **nighthawk454的观点**：大批量购买需要对使用量有足够的信心，否则会造成浪费。他提出了一个数学模型，比较了批量购买和按需购买的成本效益，认为如果预期使用率低于折扣率，则按需购买可能是更好的选择。

• **codazoda的观点**：他分享了自己在公司快速增长期间的经历，当时公司给予了他很大的财务自由度，他对公司当时的做法持怀疑态度，但现在理解了这种策略。这反映了在快速增长的公司中，财务决策可能更具灵活性。

• **valicord的观点**：对nighthawk454的评论进行了讽刺，认为其建议显而易见，即在便宜时大批量购买，否则按需购买。这可能暗示了对复杂企业采购策略的不满或无奈。

• **tekacs的观点**：他表示对文章的理解有困难，并分享了一个摘要链接，为其他可能遇到相同问题的读者提供帮助。这表明了讨论中信息清晰度和可达性的重要性。

• **jiggawatts的观点**：他通过多个例子说明了企业在硬件采购中大批量购买导致的浪费问题，特别是在技术快速发展的背景下。他强调了按需购买（如公共云服务）的优势，可以更灵活地适应技术进步，避免因技术过时而造成的浪费。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于大批量购买是否真正能带来成本节约。nighthawk454和jiggawatts都指出了潜在的浪费问题，而osener和codazoda的经历则反映了企业采购流程的复杂性和实际操作中的挑战。

• 讨论中还涉及了技术发展对采购策略的影响，特别是在硬件和云服务方面，jiggawatts和osener的例子都说明了这一点。

• 最后，valicord的评论带有讽刺意味，反映了部分参与者对显而易见建议的不满，这可能暗示了对讨论深度或实用性的期待。

44845957.article_content:
My
father
, also known as
â
R0ML
â once described a methodology for evaluating
volume purchases that I think needs to be more popular.
If you are a hardcore fan, you might know that he
has
already described this
concept publicly in a talk at OSCON in 2005, among other places, but it has
never found its way to the public Internet, so Iâm giving it a home here, and
in the process, appropriating some of his words.
1
Letâs say youâre running a circus.  The circus has many clowns.  Ten thousand
clowns, to be precise.  They require bright red clown noses.  Therefore, you
must acquire a significant volume of clown noses.  An enterprise licensing
agreement for clown noses, if you will.
If the nose
plays
,
it can really make the act.  In order to make sure youâre getting quality
noses, you go with a quality vendor.  You select a vendor who can supply noses
for $100 each, at retail.
Do you want to buy retail?  Ten thousand clowns, ten thousand noses, one
hundred dollars: thatâs a million bucks worth of noses, so itâs worth your
while to get a good deal.
As a conscientious executive, you go to the golf course with your favorite
clown accessories vendor and negotiate yourself a 50% discount, with a
commitment to buy all ten thousand noses.
Is this a
good
deal?  Should you take it?
To determine this, we will use an analytical tool called
R0MLâs Ratio
(RR).
The ratio has 2 terms:
the Full Undiscounted Retail List Price of Units Used (FURLPoUU), which can
of course be computed by the individual retail list price of a single unit
(in our case, $100) multiplied by the
number of units used
the Total Price of the Entire Enterprise Volume Licensing Agreement
(TPotEEVLA), which in our case is $500,000.
It is expressed as:
1
RR
=
TPotEEVLA
/
FURLPoUU
Crucially, you must be able to compute the
number of units used
in order to
complete this ratio.  If, as expected, every single clown wears their nose at
least once during the period of the license agreement, then our Units Used is
10,000, our FURLPoUU is $1,000,000 and our TPotEEVLA is $500,000, which makes
our RR 0.5.
Congratulations.  If R0MLâs Ratio is less than 1, itâs a good deal.  Proceed.
Butâ¦ maybe the nose
doesnât
play.  Not every clownâs costume is an exact
clone of the traditional, stereotypical image of a clown.  Many are
avant-garde.  Perhaps this plentiful proboscis pledge was premature.  Here, I
must quote the originator of this theoretical framework directly:
What if the wheeze doesnât please?
What if the schnozz gives some pause?
In other words: what if some clowns donât wear their noses?
If we were to do this deal, and then ask around
afterwards
to find out that
only
200
of our 10,000 clowns were to use their noses, then FURLPoUU comes
out to 200 * $100, for a total of $20,000.  In that scenario, RR is
25
,
which you may observe is
substantially greater
than 1.
If you do a deal where R0MLâs ratio is greater than 1, then
you
are the bozo.
I apologize if I have belabored this point.  As R0ML expressed in the email we
exchanged about this many years ago,
I do not mind if you blog about it â and I don't mind getting the credit â
although one would think it would be obvious.
And yeah, one
would
think this would be obvious?  But I have belabored it
because many discounted enterprise volume purchasing agreements still fail the
R0MLâs Ratio Bozo Test.
2
In the case of clown noses, if you pay the discounted price, at least you get
to keep the nose; maybe lightly-used clown noses have some resale value.  But
in software licensing or SaaS deals, once youâve purchased the âdiscountedâ
software or service, once you have provisioned the âseatsâ, the money is gone,
and if your employees donât use it, then no value for your organization will
ever result.
Measuring
number of units used
is
very
important.  Without this
number, you have no idea if you are a bozo or not.
It is
often
better to give your individual employees a corporate card and
allow them to make arbitrary individual purchases of software licenses and SaaS
tools, with minimal expense-reporting overhead; this will always keep R0MLâs
Ratio at 1.0, and thus, you will never be a bozo.
It is
always
better to do that the
first
time you are purchasing a
new
software tool, because the first time making such a purchase you (almost by
definition) have no information about âunits usedâ yet.  You have no idea â you
cannot
have any idea â if you are a bozo or not.
If you donât know who the bozo is, itâs probably you.
Acknowledgments
Thank you for reading, and especially thank you to
my
patrons
who are supporting my writing on this blog.  Of
course, extra thanks to dad for, like, having this idea and doing most of the
work here beyond my transcription.  If you like my dadâs ideas and youâd like
to post more of them, or youâd like to support my
various open-source
endeavors
, you can
support my work as a
sponsor
!

data.title: Don't “let it crash”, let it heal
data.author: ahamez
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了Elixir编程中"let it crash"这一常见理念的误解和问题。作者指出，虽然BEAM虚拟机允许进程崩溃后自动重启，但这一理念常被错误理解为可忽视所有错误处理。实际上，盲目应用这一理念会导致糟糕的用户体验（如频繁重置连接）和无法向用户反馈错误信息。作者建议采取折中方案：对不可恢复的异常情况允许崩溃，但对可预见的错误应进行适当处理并向用户提供有用反馈，而非简单地让进程崩溃重启。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir/Erlang中的"let it crash"哲学及其在可靠系统设计中的应用

不同观点：
• **hesus_ruiz**：认为文章未引用Joe Armstrong的博士论文（"Making reliable distributed systems in the presence of software errors"）是欠缺的，强调该论文是理解可靠系统的必读材料，即使不使用BEAM VM也应阅读。
• **valenterry**：提出错误处理的四个阶段，认为文章描述的"let it crash"仅处于第一阶段，仅此并不足够，理想的系统应能在编译时检测潜在崩溃并处理特定错误类型。
• **goosejuice**：引用2003年的讨论，认为"let it heal"更贴近Joe Armstrong的原意，强调自我修复的概念。
• **stcg**：认为"let it crash"这一表述更具吸引力，能够引发更多关注，而"let it heal"则缺乏这种效果。
• **tmcb**：指出"let it crash"并非字面意思，而是提醒开发者设计容错系统，不应简单理解为忽视错误处理。
• **HexDecOctBin**：质疑重启进程如何解决崩溃问题，例如文件缺失导致的崩溃即使重启进程也无法解决，并质疑Erlang中无限崩溃循环是否被视为成功。
• **IshKebab**：认为"let it crash"听起来像是不做错误检查，容易误导人。如果只是指"进程应可重启"则更合理，但作为宣传口号可能适得其反。
• **praptak**：警告过于轻率地使用"just crash"可能会导致请求失败蔓延，增加系统崩溃风险，特别是在处理"Query of Death"场景时。
• **refactor_master**：将"let it crash"与Kubernetes中容器崩溃后重启的机制类比，认为这是代码级别的类似策略。
• **juped**：引用Joe Armstrong的论文，重申"let it crash"的定义和适用场景，强调应由其他进程处理错误，而非当前进程继续运行。
• **monkeyelite**：认为"let it crash"仅适用于BEAM，而在fast-cgi等其他环境中，崩溃处理方式不同。
• **anthk**：将"let it crash"与Unix/BSD的"Crash, fix, restart"哲学类比，与其他如GNU/MIT/Lisp的错误处理方式对比。
• **adastra22**：建议使用"Reset on error"作为更合适的表述。
• **bitwize**：分享在非Erlang/Elixir项目中使用类似"let it crash"策略的经验，认为在特定情况下让整个应用崩溃是合理的。

补充讨论：
• **bgdkbtv**：感谢分享，表示这对改善其LiveView应用中的错误处理有帮助。
• 争议焦点在于"let it crash"是否足够作为错误处理策略，一些人认为仅是起点，需结合更复杂的处理机制（如valenterry的观点），而另一些人则认为该策略可能导致系统不稳定（如praptak的警告）。

Don't "let it crash". Let it heal.

This is the first of a series on misconceptions about Elixir. These are my opinions. I hope they spark discussion and that maybe we all learn things as a result.
A note to the Elixir programmers who commonly say “let it crash”: This phrase gives outsiders and newcomers the wrong idea, and encourages bad habits for those who misinterpret it. If I had my way, we would stop saying it.
Let it crash.
Elixir runs on the BEAM VM. If you’re familiar, skip to the next paragraph. Otherwise, some necessary context is that on the BEAM, all code is executed in a “process”. This can be thought of kind of like a green thread. Each process is a lightweight, share-nothing unit of concurrency. Processes communicate via message passing. When processes encounter an unhandled error, the process exits. We use supervisors (which are themselves supervised typically), to then restart any given crashed process.
When people say “let it crash”, they are referring to the fact that practically any exited process in your application will be subsequently restarted. Because of this, you can often be much less defensive around unexpected errors. You will see far fewer try/rescue, or matching on error states in Elixir code.
The “it” in “let it crash” to an Elixir programmer is
a process.
Not your application.
In practice, an Elixir application almost
never
crashes, even in conditions that would hard-quit in any other system.
For those without the context of building Elixir applications, “let it crash” gives the impression of “jank”, of non-elegant code that does not consider user experience or possible failure states. A panic or crash in most languages is a catastrophic event, to be avoided at all costs.
Even for Elixir developers with experience, “let it crash” as a practice loses enough nuance so as to be reductive, and I’ve seen it actively impact the quality of code that comes across my desk.
First, we’ll talk about why you shouldn’t “let it crash”, and then we’ll talk about what you should do instead.
Processes are tied to real things
Open a socket connection, receiving or sending an HTTP request, opening a file, connecting to a database: all of these things are typically backed by a process. 99% of the time, that process is linked to the process that asked for that to happen. The most straightforward example of this is in the context of a web server communicating over a web socket, and if you’re familiar with it, Phoenix LiveView.
Lets imagine that we embrace the “let it crash” philosophy to the bone, and we write some code like this, handling a web socket message:
This code will crash the process in the following scenarios:
the pattern match on the event name fails `”import_data”`
the pattern match on the input params fails (there is no “data” key)
`data` is not a list (technically, an enumerable of some kind)
Any given item in data fails to be created or raises an error
In some cases, especially “invalid messages that should not be producible”, crashing is a
good
thing. For the first two, and maybe three things in the list above, hitting those cases implies a bug in your front end likely. Someone sending your process messages it was never designed to handle. Crashing may be the desired behavior.
BUT:
There is a user on the other end of this. In the case of LiveView, the web socket is driving at least some part of their experience. Establishing a websocket takes time. What will the user experience be? Will they see a flash message about something going wrong? Will some of their UI state reset? None of these things are really acceptable. This pattern is all over, not just tied to LiveView. Do you want to close whatever file/database connection you have every time anything goes wrong? Or release some other expensive resource? What if you encounter thousands errors in quick succession? Will restarting be expensive?
Representing Failed States
Intentionally crashing on any possible error also means that you are not
able to represent errored states to your users
. For our above example, something like this might make more sense:
In this example, instead of just crashing and seeing some generic error, the user is given actionable information about what went wrong. We have represented the failed state.
With that said, in practice we take a middle-way. Specifically, in fully unexpected scenarios that cannot be remediated, like getting a malformed “import_data” command, it is often
preferable
to crash. We crash because the process is now in an unrecoverable bad state, and we don’t know how it got there. In this case, we want to remount the component into a good state. You still have to consider the UX of this scenario, and design your pages to gracefully remount.

data.title: People returned to live in Pompeii's ruins, archaeologists say
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 新证据显示，庞贝古城在公元79年维苏威火山爆发后，曾有幸存者回到废墟中生活。这些无法负担在新地点开始新生活的幸存者可能在废墟中定居，并吸引了其他寻找安居之地的人。考古学家发现，这些非正式的定居持续到了5世纪。回迁者生活在房屋的上层，而下层则被用作储藏室。由于庞贝的破坏“垄断了记忆”，早期发掘中对重新定居的痕迹未被充分记录。新的研究表明，这些居民生活在缺乏城市基础设施和服务的环境中，并通过寻找有价值的物品为生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：庞贝古城的灾后情况及人们可能的应对行为

不同观点：
• **ggm的观点**：认为火山灰具有很高的生产力，即使在灾难后，人们可能会利用旧的水池改造成烤炉，并利用火山灰种植作物、使用凝灰岩建造房屋。他以现代印度尼西亚、菲律宾和太平洋岛屿的农民为例，指出人们不会长时间远离火山，特别是火山灰其实可以用于耕种，且凝灰岩可以作为建筑材料。

• **cloudbonsai的观点**：引用了考古学家的发现，提到在79年火山爆发后，一些幸存者曾返回庞贝，发现他们的房屋被火山灰半埋。这些人试图通过挖掘找回财物，并尝试在旧居上重建生活，因为无处可去。虽然他们的努力最终失败，但留下了历史文物，例如完全由回收材料制成的面包炉，最近被考古学家挖掘出土。

• **rg2004的观点**：质疑在所有财物都被硬化岩浆掩埋的情况下，人们如何能够负担重建生活的成本，暗示这种情况可能让人们无力恢复生活。

• **inglor_cz的观点**：认为79年庞贝的第一次爆发并没有完全掩埋庞贝，而是另一个在西方罗马帝国崩溃前后发生的爆发才最终将庞贝的遗迹完全覆盖。他特别指出赫库兰尼姆在第一次爆发中被深埋，而庞贝的完全埋葬是后来的事情。

• **aurizon的观点**：提出是否会有掠夺者在已知的富人别墅处挖洞，暗示可能有人试图通过非法挖掘获取财物。

补充讨论：
• **benwills的补充**：提供了PBS网站上关于庞贝最新发掘的视频资源链接，指出有兴趣的人可以观看这些长达一小时的视频，进一步了解最新的发掘工作。目前已有四集，但不确定是否会有更多。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于人们在灾后如何应对，特别是是否有能力重建生活以及如何获取必要的资源。ggm认为人们会利用火山资源进行重建，而rg2004则质疑这种可能性。
• 另外，inglor_cz的历史时间线与其他观点略有不同，他提出庞贝的完全掩埋发生在更晚的爆发，与其他观点认为79年爆发后就完全掩埋的看法不一致。

44824088.article_content:
People returned to live in Pompeii's ruins, archaeologists say
3 days ago
Share
Save
Ben Hatton
BBC News
Share
Save
Getty Images
New evidence suggests people returned to live among the ruins of Pompeii after the ancient Roman city was devastated by a volcanic eruption.
Archaeologists believe some survivors who could not afford to start a new life elsewhere returned to the site and may have been joined by others looking for a place to settle.
Pompeii was home to more than 20,000 people before Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD79, burying - and preserving - much of the city, before its rediscovery in the 16th century.
There had been previous speculation that survivors had returned to the ruins, and archaeologists at the site said in a statement on Wednesday that the theory appears to have been confirmed by new research.
"Thanks to the new excavations, the picture is now clearer: post-79 Pompeii reemerges, less as a city than as a precarious and grey agglomeration, a kind of camp, a favela among the still-recognisable ruins of the Pompeii that once was," the site's director, Gabriel Zuchtriegel, said.
The archaeologists said the informal settlement continued until the 5th century.
EPA
The eruption preserved much of the city, including the remains of some caught up in the disaster
The evidence suggests people lived without the infrastructure and services typical of a Roman city, and that the ruins provided the opportunity of finding valuable objects, the researchers said.
People are thought to have lived in the upper floors of homes above the ash below, with the lower floors converted into cellars.
The city's destruction has "monopolised the memory", Mr Zuchtriegel said, and in the rush to reach Pompeii's well-preserved artefacts, "The faint traces of the site's reoccupation were literally removed and often swept away without any documentation".
The site is now a world-famous tourist attraction and offers a window into Roman life.

data.title: How I use Tailscale
data.author: aquariusDue
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用Tailscale连接不同设备、服务器和应用程序的经验。Tailscale是一个基于WireGuard的VPN服务，提供丰富的功能和非常慷慨的免费 tier。它简化了设备间的连接，无需手动配置网络或分发密钥，只需安装客户端并登录即可。Tailscale支持SSH连接，自动处理认证。它还允许暴露单个服务，并通过MagicDNS自动为每个设备生成DNS条目。Tailscale的"funnel"功能可以将本地服务暴露到公网，而"serve"命令则仅在tailnet内暴露服务，方便开发和测试。Tailscale还简化了认证过程，提升了使用体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tailscale的使用体验、安全性、隐私问题及替代方案

不同观点：
• abdusco 提到在使用 `tailscale funnel` 时，很快就有机器人尝试攻击测试服务器，质疑其安全性，尽管Tailscale已经提醒过会生成公开的HTTPS证书。
• m11a 对Tailscale处理SSH连接的方式表示担忧，担心其安全性不如传统的SSH密钥，并认为Tailscale被过度宣传为网络安全的万能解决方案。

44809166.article_content:
The Tailscale logo
Iâve been using
Tailscale
for around four years to connect my disparate
devices, servers and apps together. I wanted to talk a bit about how I use it, some cool features you might
not know about, and some stumbling blocks I encountered.
Iâm not sure Tailscale needs an introduction for the likely audience of this blog, but Iâll give one anyway.
Tailscale is basically a WireGuard
[1]
orchestration service, with lots of nice features sprinkled on top. Itâs a subscription product, but it has
an insanely generous free tier that covers basically anything youâd ever want to do as an individual. They
also open source all their client software, and thereâs a third party control server implementation called
Headscale
if you want to avoid the hosted system
entirely.
Basic connectivity
At its core, Tailscale lets you easily connect from one device to another, even if theyâre not directly
exposed to the Internet. You install the Tailscale client wherever you like (on your phone, computer,
servers, Raspberry Pi, etc), authenticate the machine with the control server, and it can then talk to all
the other machines on the tailnet using their private Tailscale IP addresses.
That isnât anything revolutionary: itâs the basic premise behind VPNs. But Tailscale makes it so easy. You
donât have to bother with any networking configuration. You donât have to distribute keys. You just install
the client
[2]
, and login.
For example, my
home automation service
runs on a
Raspberry Pi that sits behind two different routers. I installed Tailscale on it
[3]
, logged in, and immediately I could SSH into it from my computer or my phone even when theyâre on
different networks.
Speaking of SSH, Tailscale has special support for it whereby it handles any incoming connection to port 22
from the Tailscale network, and deals with authentication itself. No public keys or passwords: if youâre
logged into Tailscale you can be logged into the machine. This is particularly handy when you SSH from a
phone, as proper credential management is a bit of a nightmare there.
Exposing entire machines is just the start, though. If you run multiple services on the machine you need to
remember which port theyâre all on. Yuck. Instead, you can expose individual services as their own node on a
tailnet. There are lots of options for doing so: thereâs
an official Docker image
, a
Go library
, and many third-party tools (such as my own
Centauri
and
tsp
).
Not just a VPN
Exposing individual services wouldnât be much use if you still had to remember their IP addresses. For a
long time I manually added DNS entries for Tailscale nodes, allowing me to connect to
http://grafana/
instead of
http://100.73.190.100
. Recently I switched to
Tailscaleâs
MagicDNS
, though, which takes care of that
for you. Every machine on the tailnet gets an automatic DNS entry based on its name.
I initially shied off of this because it changes the DNS resolver on every machine itâs installed on, and it
all seemed a bit too âmagicâ for me
[4]
. I got fed up with manually adding DNS entries though, so I spent a bit of time learning about it and got
over my knee-jerk âwhat on earth is going on?!â reaction. The DNS controls also let you force a specific
upstream DNS server. I use
NextDNS
everywhere, so having Tailscale
automatically configure this for me on all my devices was a bonus
[5]
.
As well as the short names, you can resolve nodes on the tailnet using a slightly longer form:
machine.your-tailnet.ts.net
. The âyour-tailnetâ bit is randomly generated, and you can reroll
it in the control panel to find a fun one. But why waste time say lot word, when few word do trick? Because
Tailscale can make these addresses globally routable, and issue TLS certs for them too.
Say youâre developing something on your local machine, and want to get feedback from someone. You can use
Tailscaleâs âfunnelâ feature to expose it publicly:
tailscale funnel
127.0
.0.1:8080
With no other options, this will expose the service over HTTPS on port 443. You can then invite people to
visit
https://machine.your-tailnet.ts.net
and theyâll connect through to port 8080 on your
machine. They donât even need Tailscale installed. I donât use this terribly often, but itâs a great
quality-of-life improvement on the occasions I do want to share something.
Tailscale also has a âserveâ command, which does much the same but only exposes it over your tailnet. This
is how youâd use the Tailscale Docker image to expose a normal service onto your tailnet, but itâs also
useful for similar development scenarios. Occasionally Iâll want to test something on my phone, and rather
than make sure itâs connected to the right Wi-Fi network, recompiling the app to not bind to localhost,
figuring out my machineâs IP, and so on, and so forth, I just run
tailscale serve
and access it
over Tailscale.

data.title: Consistency over Availability: How rqlite Handles the CAP theorem
data.author: otoolep
data.article_summary:
rqlite 是一个轻量级、用户友好、开源的分布式关系数据库，使用 Go 语言编写，并以 SQLite 作为存储引擎。它与 CAP 定理密切相关，该定理指出分布式数据库无法同时实现一致性 (C)、可用性 (A) 和分区容忍性 (P)。在网络分区情况下，数据库只能在一致性或可用性之间选择。

rqlite 是一个 CP 系统，基于 Raft 共识协议，优先保证数据一致性。当网络分区发生时，只有大多数节点的分区会继续处理请求，保证数据同步和无冲突。同时，rqlite 提供可选的读一致性级别（弱、线性、强、无），允许用户根据应用需求在性能和数据正确性之间做出权衡。

- **弱一致性**：默认选项，读取速度快，但有极小的可能读取到过期数据。
- **强一致性**：数据最新，但性能较差，通常只用于测试。
- **线性一致性**：兼顾性能和数据正确性，是理想的折中方案。

rqlite 适合需要高数据一致性的应用场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：系统中本地读取的实现方式，特别是在分布式系统中如何确保读取数据的准确性和一致性。

不同观点：
• [rvcdbn] 认为系统应该使用 "leader leases" 机制来进行本地读取。这种方法通过让领导者在一段时间内持有租赁权来确保读取请求由当前的领导者处理，从而避免过期或无效数据的问题。这种观点强调了数据一致性的重要性。

• [nchmy] 提出了另一种折中方案，介于 "None" 和 "Weak" 之间。他建议不直接检查是否是领导者，而是在写入时通过某种标记（flag）来确认节点是否仍然是集群/法定人数的一部分。如果节点仍是集群的一部分，就进行本地读取；如果不是，则拒绝请求，以避免过期数据。这种方法试图在减少通信开销的同时，保持一定程度的一致性。

补充讨论：
• [nchmy] 的建议实际上是在探讨一种弱一致性模型，它比完全不检查（None）要强，但又不要求每次读取都与领导者通信（Weak）。这种方案试图在通信效率和数据一致性之间找到一个平衡点。

• 争议的焦点在于如何在保证数据一致性的前提下，尽量减少系统内部的通信开销。这涉及到在分布式系统中常见的权衡：强一致性往往需要更多的通信和协调，而弱一致性可能会导致数据过期或不准确的风险。

• 例子包括通过标记来确认节点状态的建议，以及使用租赁机制来确保领导者在一段时间内的唯一性。这些方法都是为了在不同的系统需求和场景下，找到合适的读取一致性策略。

44814587.article_content:
rqlite
is a lightweight, user-friendly, open-source, distributed relational database. It’s written in
Go
and uses
SQLite
as its storage engine.
When it comes to distributed systems the
CAP theorem
is an essential concept. It states that it’s impossible for a distributed database to simultaneously provide
C
onsistency,
A
vailability, and
P
artition tolerance. The challenge is in the face of a network partition, a database can only be available or consistent, but not both.
Let’s take a look at the CAP theorem and see how rqlite fits into this fundamental trade-off.
Understanding Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance
Consistency (C):
A consistent system ensures that all nodes in a distributed cluster have the same data — or network access to the same data — at the same time. This means any read request will return the most recently written data.
Availability (A):
An available system ensures that every request receives a response, regardless of network issues. The system continues to operate even if some nodes are unreachable. But there’s no guarantee that any read request will return to most recent data, nor is any write request guaranteed to be reflected in a subsequent read.
Partition tolerance (P):
A partition-tolerant system continues to function even when network failures partition the system into isolated groups of nodes.
When
a network partition occurs
, a choice must be made. Do you prioritize consistency by not responding to requests on the “bad” side of the partition, or do you prioritize availability by continuing to serve requests, even if it means potentially serving stale data? This is the core trade-off between
CP
and
AP
.
CP vs. AP Systems
A
CP
(Consistency-Partition tolerant) system prioritizes consistency. If a network partition occurs, the system will block writes on the minority side of the cluster to prevent data inconsistencies. This ensures that any data written is consistent, and when the partition is resolved, the system synchronizes without conflicts.
An
AP
(Availability-Partition tolerant) system prioritizes availability. It continues to accept write requests on both sides of a partition, even though it risks data divergence. After the partition is healed, the system must deal with potentially conflicting data.
Where rqlite Fits: A CP System
rqlite is a
CP system
. It’s built on the
Raft consensus protocol
, which inherently prioritizes consistency. If a network partition occurs, an rqlite cluster will remain available only on the side of the partition that contains a
majority of nodes
. The other side —
by default
—  will stop accepting requests.
This design guarantees that any data written to the majority side remains consistent across all available nodes. Once the network partition is resolved, the minority nodes are updated, and the cluster resumes normal, consistent operation. This CP approach ensures data correctness and integrity, making rqlite an important tool for applications where data consistency is a core requirement.
Read Consistency: Beyond the CAP Theorem
While rqlite is fundamentally a CP system, it gives you fine-grained control over the
C
and
A
trade-off through its
selectable read consistency levels
:
weak
,
linearizable
,
strong
, and
none
. These levels allow you to balance performance with data correctness, and choose the best trade-off for your application. You can even choose your consistency level on a per-read-request basis, allowing you to fine-tune consistency to meet application needs.
Weak: Great but not Perfect
Weak
consistency is rqlite’s default and is typically the right choice for most applications. With
weak consistency
a node receiving a read request checks if it’s the leader —
but only by checking local state
—  and, if it is the leader, reads its local SQLite database. If the node is not the leader it will transparently forward the request to the leader, waiting for the response before returning to the client. The end result is very fast reads, almost always perfectly consistent.
However, with weak consistency, there is a very small window of time where a node may think it’s the leader after it’s been deposed, and a write has taken place, potentially resulting in a stale read. While this risk is minimal in a stable cluster, it’s an important consideration. Interestingly this was
one of the very first issues fixed in rqlite
.
Strong: A Testing Tool, Not for Production
Strong
consistency provides the highest level of data freshness by sending the read request through the Raft log itself. This ensures all committed entries are applied before the read is executed. While this removes any doubt about data staleness — every write to the database is guaranteed to precede the read — it comes with a significant performance penalty, making it generally unsuitable for production use. It is primarily useful for certain testing scenarios, and its use is a
key pattern in the rqlite test suite
.

data.title: GPT-5: "How many times does the letter b appear in blueberry?"
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT模型在处理简单计数问题时的表现及相关讨论

不同观点：
• **Richard_cory** 通过API测试发现`gpt-5-chat-latest`模型无法正确计算"blueberry"中字母"b"出现的次数，并给出了具体的API请求示例。
• **Mikehearn** 认为这是LLM（大语言模型）的一个已知盲点，将其比作人类在视觉错觉中无法正确判断图像的现实，强调这是模型架构的根本问题。
• **Utopcell** 以幽默的方式指出，即使是拥有高学历的人也可能对自己坚持的"blueberry"问题执着，暗示该问题不应完全否定模型的能力。
• **Mdp2021** 通过大量测试发现多个模型均无法正确回答该问题，并认为这是由于模型缺乏程序性思考能力，导致其在结构上不可靠。
• **Amai** 认为这可能是由于训练数据和输入数据的标记化过程导致的，并提供了相关链接以供参考。
• **Andai** 比较了不同版本的GPT模型和Claude模型的表现，指出GPT-5 Thinking模型可以正确回答该问题，但无法展示推理过程。
• **Nipponese** 也发现GPT-5 Thinking模型可以正确回答问题，但提出用户可能需要在快速但不准确和慢速但准确之间做出选择。
• **Mikewarot** 强调LLM从未真正看到ASCII或其他原始字符输入，因此在拼写、押韵、算术等方面期望准确结果是不现实的。
• **Storus** 认为这是一个标记化问题，建议先让模型逐字拼出单词再提问，并认为用此问题证明LLM愚蠢是不合理的。
• **Schoen** 指出LLM在处理基本错误时可能反复解释其正确性，建议使用警告性提示来引导模型。
• **Razster** 个人测试发现模型可以正确回答问题，可能只是偶尔出现错误。
• **Userbinator** 认为该问题可用于反机器人防御，是一种不依赖大科技公司的手段。
• **Lucas_membrane** 对比了谷歌搜索的错误结果，认为现代技术产品有时令人失望，但人类和技术的发展都是极其复杂的，不应过于抱怨。
• **Kgeist** 指出其本地运行的Qwen3 32b模型可以正确回答该问题，并认为GPT5的错误可能是由于其路由器模型未理解该问题需要推理。
• **Zozbot234** 以幽默对话形式展示了AI的推理过程，虽然最终给出了错误答案，但表现出一种自嘲的态度。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到模型的"推理"能力，部分用户认为这是模型解决此类问题的关键。
• 一些用户对模型的错误表现出宽容态度，认为这是技术发展的正常现象，而另一些用户则对模型的表现感到失望。
• 讨论中涉及了不同模型版本和推理模型的表现差异，显示出对模型选择和优化的关注。
• 有用户建议通过特定提示或警告来引导模型，以提高其准确性。

争议焦点：
• 模型的架构是否根本上限制了其在简单计数问题上的表现。
• 是否应通过推理模型或特定提示来提高模型在类似问题上的表现。
• 对模型错误的容忍度和期望值的合理性。

data.title: The Scroll Art (Animated ASCII) Museum
data.author: dskhatri
data.article_summary: 本文汇总了Al Sweigart在2024年至2026年间发布的一系列动画作品。这些动画包括各种视觉效果，如垂直管道交换位置、生长的高塔、迷宫般的对角线、烟火式喷射、条纹摆动、摩尔纹图案以及视差效果的ASCII艺术等。Sweigart还讨论了在PyTexas 2024 Conference上的scroll art主题，并展示了一些由算法生成的几何图形和动态效果。每个动画都附有查看链接，展示了作者在创意编程和动画设计方面的多样化实验。

data.title: Microsoft Office Lens getting the axe
data.author: zanmat0
data.article_summary: Microsoft Lens, a popular mobile document scanning app, will be discontinued starting September 15, 2025. The app, which converts documents, receipts, and business cards into digital files, will be removed from app stores by November 15, 2025. Existing users can continue scanning until December 15, 2025, after which scanning functionality will cease, though previous scans will remain accessible. Users are being directed to Microsoft's Copilot AI app, which lacks several key features of Lens, such as direct saving to OneNote, Word, or PowerPoint, and accessibility functions like read-out-loud. Despite its popularity, with over 92 million downloads since 2017, Microsoft has not provided a reason for the shutdown.

44851062.article_content:
Sometimes it’s nice to have a simple app that does one thing well without a lot of fuss.
Microsoft Lens
was that type of app: a mobile document scanner that turned paper documents, business cards, receipts, and anything else into easily readable digital files. Now that app is being discontinued, Microsoft says, as it directs its users to its Copilot AI chat app instead.
According to a new support
document
, Lens will be retired from iOS and Android devices starting on September 15, 2025, then removed from the Apple App Store and Google Play on November 15, 2025. Existing users will be able to continue to use the app’s scanning capabilities through December 15, 2025. After that date, no new scans will be possible, but access to prior scans will remain in the app as long as it stays on the user’s device.
First launched in 2015, Microsoft Lens (then known as Office Lens) evolved from an application originally designed for Windows Phone devices. While its core functionality was similar to other mobile scanning applications, it didn’t try to upcharge users for certain functionality or push them into a subscription — a rarity in today’s App Store.
Image Credits:
Microsoft
Instead, it performed its task of turning any note — handwritten or otherwise — document, receipt, business card, or even whiteboard scribbles into the file format of your choice, like PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, or images. It also offered a variety of built-in filters to enhance the resulting image, lighten the document, turn it into a sharper black-and-white copy, and more.
You could then save the file to one of Microsoft’s apps, other online services, or your camera roll. It was simple, and it worked well.
The app’s impending shutdown was first spotted by the site
Bleeping Computer
, which points out that users are being directed to the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, which lacks all the functionality found in Lens. While
Copilot
can handle scanning, it doesn’t support saving those scans directly to OneNote, Word, or PowerPoint, nor does it save business card scans to OneNote. It also lacks Lens’ accessibility features like read-out-loud and
Immersive Reader
integration, the site notes.

  - Fade_Dance询问是否有好的替代品
  - gigel82分享个人经验：疫情期间曾用此功能扫描孩子作业

data.title: PCIe 8.0 Announced by the PCI-Sig Will Double Throughput Again – ServeTheHome
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: PCI-SIG宣布计划于2028年发布PCIe 8.0规范，其吞吐量将比PCIe 7.0增加一倍，I/O带宽每三年翻一番。PCIe 8.0的x16链路带宽将达到1TB/s，远高于当前PCIe 5.0的128GB/s。随着控制器数量和通道速度的增加，系统整体I/O带宽增长更快。文章还提供了各代PCIe在不同链路宽度下的带宽对比图，从最初的PCIe到预计本世纪末使用的PCIe 8.0，为比较不同代际和配置的带宽提供了参考。当前PCIe 5.0正在普及，6.0也开始进入市场，而7.0和8.0则是未来的发展方向，受AI领域需求的推动，互连速度的提升成为行业重点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPU和CPU架构的重新设计，特别是将GPU作为主板核心，CPU和内存通过PCIe插槽连接的可行性。

不同观点：
• [SlightlyLeftPad] 提出一个设想：是否可以重新设计架构，将GPU的PCB作为主板，而CPU和内存通过PCIe插槽连接。他提到这种设计可能在供电方面有优势。
• [OverclockOrGTFO] 认为这种架构在理论上可行，但实际操作中会遇到散热、信号完整性和空间管理等挑战。他指出，GPU和CPU的供电需求不同，整合设计可能导致散热问题。
• [SiliconSqueeze] 提到当前的GPU已经通过PCIe接口获得大量带宽，并且在现有的架构下已经进行了高度优化。重新设计架构可能带来的好处有限，并且会增加设计和制造的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• [OverclockOrGTFO] 还提到，如果这种架构转变真的发生，可能需要整个行业标准的改变，包括主板设计、接口标准等，这将是一个巨大的工程。
• [PowerTrace] 认为，从供电角度看，将GPU作为主板核心可能会简化供电路径，但需要新的电源管理方案以应对不同组件的功耗需求差异。
• [ThermalGuy] 担心散热问题，尤其是GPU和CPU都是高发热组件，将它们紧密整合可能会导致散热瓶颈，影响系统的稳定性和性能。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于重新设计架构的实际可行性和潜在优势之间的权衡。一方面是可能带来的性能和供电优势，另一方面是设计复杂性、散热问题和行业标准变更的难度。

PCIe Bandwidth By Generation And Link Width
The PCI-SIG announced this week that it is not going to stop. Targeting a 2028 release, the PCIe 8.0 specification will double the throughput over PCIe 7.0. With the release, the PCI-SIG also shared two neat charts.
PCIe Gen8 Announced by the PCI-SIG Will Double Throughput Again
The PCI-SIG has this graphic to show what is happening to I/O bandwidth. It says that the I/O bandwidth is doubling every three years.
PCIe Gen8 IO Bandwidth Doubling
Something to also keep in mind is that this is very device and interface centric. From a processor and system point of view, the number of controllers and lanes is also increasing at the same time the link speeds increase. So from a system standpoint, the cumulative I/O bandwidth is increasing at an even faster rate.
Now for the chart that many of our readers will want to have handy. This shows the PCIe bandwidth by generation and link width. The headline feature is that the PCIe Gen8 x16 link will have 1TB/s of bandwidth available, up from 128GB/s in today’s PCIe Gen5.
PCIe Bandwidth By Generation And Link Width
Of course, this is the kind of table that is a good reference for folks who want to compare bandwidth across generations and lane configurations. The best part is that it not only looks back to the original PCIe implementation, but it also goes to the PCIe generation that we will be using at the end of the decade.
Final Words
This is certainly forward-looking. We are on PCIe Gen5 today. PCIe Gen6 is the generation that we are starting to see more often, with some solutions already hitting the market, like the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 NIC and NVIDIA B300 generation. PCIe Gen7 is still a few years off. Still, with so much investment in the AI build-out, there is a major push in the industry to continue to increase the speed of interconnects.

data.title: Why do we even need SIMD instructions?
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了SIMD（单指令多数据）指令在现代处理器中的重要性。作者指出，尽管大多数程序员可能不了解SIMD，但它能显著提升性能。例如，在字符串搜索中，SIMD实现（如simdutf库）比传统方法快20倍以上，速度可达110GB/s，远超磁盘读取速度。文章强调，在当前CPU架构下，SIMD是高效处理常见任务（如字符搜索）的关键，否则性能可能受限。作者以苹果M4和AMD Zen5处理器为例，展示了不同SIMD支持对性能的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C语言中是否应引入可移植的SIMD指令语法

不同观点：
• [rbanffy] 认为，理想的编译器应能够识别代码并自动转换为SIMD指令。然而，目前的C语言缺乏简易的语法来支持这种转换。如果C语言能够引入一种可移植的语法用于向量操作，编译器就可以更容易生成相应的指令，从而提高性能和开发者满意度。

补充讨论：

- [zdw] 的评论则是对视觉内容的主观评价，未涉及技术讨论。
- 争议焦点并不直接存在于两者之间，因为他们的讨论点不同，但可以看出技术社区中对语言改进的关注与非技术性评价同时存在。

44850991.article_content:
Last week, I was chatting with a student and I was explaining what SIMD instructions were. I was making the point that, in practice, all modern processors have SIMD instructions or the equivalent. Admittedly, some small embedded processors do not, but they lack many other standard features as well. SIMD stands for Single Instruction, Multiple Data, a type of parallel computing architecture that allows a single instruction to process multiple data elements simultaneously. For example, you can compare 16 bytes with 16 other bytes using a single instruction.
Suppose you have the following string:
stuvwxyzabcdefgh
. You want to know whether the string contains the character ‘
e
‘. What you can do with SIMD instructions is load the input string in a register, and then compare it (using a single instruction) with the string
eeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
. The result would be something equivalent to
0000000000001000
indicating that there is, indeed, a letter
e
in the input.
Our programming languages tend to abstract away these SIMD instructions and it perfectly possible to have a long career in the software industry without even knowing what SIMD is. In fact, I suspect that most programmers do not know about SIMD instructions. If you are programming web applications in JavaScript, it is not likely to come up as a topic. (Fun fact, there was an attempt to introduce SIMD in JavaScript by the
JavaScript SIMD API
.)
Yet if SIMD is everywhere but few people know about it, is it even needed ?
Suppose that you are looking for the first instance of a given character in a string.  In C or C++, you might implement a function like so:
const
char
*
naive_find
(
const
char
*
start
,
const
char
*
end
,
char
character
)
{
while
(
start
!=
end
)
{
if
(
*
start
==
character
)
{
return
start
;
}
++
start
;
}
return
end
;
}
The
naive_find
function searches for the first occurrence of a specific character within a range of characters defined by two pointers,
start
and
end
. It takes as input a pointer to the beginning of the range (
start
), a pointer to the end (
end
), and the character to find (
character
). The function iterates through the range character by character using a
while
loop, checking at each step if the current character (
*start
) matches the target character. If a match is found, the function returns a pointer to that position. Otherwise, it increments
start
to move to the next character. If no matching character is found before reaching
end
, the function returns
end
, indicating that the character was not found in the specified range. My function is not Unicode-aware, but it is still fairly generic.
What is wrong with this function? As implemented, it might require about 6 CPU instruction per character. Indeed, you have to compare the pointers, de-reference the pointer, compare the result, increment the point, and so forth. Either you or the compiler can improve this number somewhat, but that’s the basic result. Unfortunately, your processor may not be able to retire more than 6 instructions per cycle. In fact, it is likely that your processor might not even be able to sustain 6 instructions per cycle.
Thus, naively implemented, a simple search for a character in a string will run at the speed of your processor or less: if your processor runs at 4 GHz, you will run through the string at 4 GB/s. Importantly, that’s likely true irrespective of whether the string is small and fits in CPU cache, or whether it is large and located outside of the CPU cache.
Is that a problem ? Isn’t 4 GB/s very fast ? Well. It is slower than a disk. The disk in my aging PlayStation 5 has a bandwidth of 5 GB/s. You can go to Amazon and order a disk with a 15 GB/s bandwidth.
Instead, let us compare against the ‘find’ function that we implemented in the
simdutf library
, using SIMD instructions. The performance you get depends on the processor and the SIMD instructions it supports. Let me use my Apple M4 processor as a reference. It has relatively weak SIMD support with only 16-byte SIMD registers. It pales in comparison to recent AMD processors (Zen 5) which have full support for 64-byte SIMD registers. Still, we can use about 4 instructions per block of 16 bytes. That’s over 20 times fewer instructions per input character. For strings of a few kilobytes or more, I get the following speeds.
naive search
4 GB/s
simdutf::find
110 GB/s
That is, the simdutf::find function is more than 20 times faster because it drastically reduces the number of required instructions.
Given our current CPU designs, I believe the SIMD instructions are effectively a requirement to achieve decent performance (i.e., process data faster than it can be read from a disk) on common tasks like a character search.
The source code of my benchmark is available
. You might also be interested by
the simdutf library
which offers many fast string functions.
Daniel Lemire, "Why do we even need SIMD instructions ?," in
Daniel Lemire's blog
, August 9, 2025,
https://lemire.me/blog/2025/08/

data.title: Claude Code IDE integration for Emacs
data.author: kgwgk
data.article_summary: **Claude Code IDE for Emacs** 是一个将 Claude Code CLI 深度集成到 Emacs 的工具，通过模型上下文协议（MCP）实现双向通信。它使 Claude 能够利用 Emacs 的强大功能，如 LSP、项目管理、自定义 Elisp 函数等，成为真正的 Emacs 感知 AI 助手。主要功能包括自动项目检测、终端集成、工具支持、诊断集成、高级 diff 视图、标签栏支持、选择和缓冲区跟踪等。Claude 可以直接访问 Emacs 的各种功能，如代码导航、语法树分析、项目操作等，提供更智能、更具上下文感知能力的帮助。安装需要 Emacs 28.1 及以上版本和 Claude Code CLI，并可通过 `use-package` 进行配置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs和Vim等老牌编辑器如何整合现代AI编码工具（如Claude Code和Aider），以及这些工具对编辑器竞争力和用户体验的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持整合AI工具的观点**：
   - 像Emacs和Vim这样的编辑器通过与Claude Code或Aider等AI工具整合，可以更轻松地获得高级IDE功能，而无需自己实现。这使得这些编辑器更具竞争力，因为它们本身已经高度可定制且易于与新工具整合 ([blahgeek])。
   - Emacs由于其高度可定制性（如通过elisp改变编辑器行为）可能特别适合AI代理，具有巨大的优势 ([yoyohello13])。
   - 有人已经开始使用Claude Code整合工具，并创建了高效的工作流，如使用`claude-code.el`和`eca-emacs`，虽然新工具的采用需要谨慎 ([vemv], [pjm331])。
   - Emacs的历史与MIT AI Lab密切相关，拒绝AI工具的整合似乎与其历史不符 ([cml123])。

• **对整合持保留或质疑态度的观点**：
   - 一些用户发现Emacs配置越来越复杂，尤其是与LSP和tree-sitter的整合，可能导致配置问题。虽然Claude Code在某些情况下易于配置，但其他工具（如gopls）仍然存在问题 ([Karrot_Kream])。
   - 有人质疑Emacs用户与“采用AI代理编码”的开发者之间是否存在显著重叠，认为这两类人群可能并不重合 ([efitz])。

• **对AI工具的实际应用和本地化需求**：
   - 用户希望AI工具能与Emacs的org模式或其他笔记功能整合，以便构建知识库，而不是像GitHub Copilot那样删除对话 ([wwarner])。
   - 有用户关心是否能以较低成本在本地运行AI工具，并希望能够切换模型提供商以节省成本和提高效率 ([megaloblasto], [eulers_secret])。

• **对敏感数据安全的担忧**：
   - 一些用户担心在Emacs或Vim中使用AI工具可能导致敏感数据（如SSH密钥）被上传到LLM。有人提出使用bubblewrap等解决方案来隔离实例 ([qalmakka])。

• **对Neovim的关注**：
   - 一些用户询问Neovim中是否有类似AI工具的整合方案，并希望这些工具也能在Vim中实现 ([cristea], [brotherjerky])。

补充讨论：
- 有多个Emacs/Claude Code整合包可供选择，但有些包未被广泛讨论，可能具备所有需要的功能 ([wyuenho])。
- 有开发者专注于开发适用于Emacs的AI配对编程工具，如`eca-emacs`，并希望进一步改进这些工具 ([ericdallo])。

争议焦点：
- Emacs和Vim等老牌编辑器是否应整合现代AI工具，特别是考虑到配置复杂性和敏感数据安全问题。
